tb21_profile.skill: Read a decompressor's source to reverse-engineer its input format, then hand-craft a valid compressed byte stream that decodes to a target file while staying under a strict size budget
tb21_profile.domain: Compression algorithms and custom binary formats in C; byte-level encoding, headers/framing, stdin/stdout pipelines
tb21_profile.task_form: reverse-engineer-a-format then implement-an-encoder under an optimise-for-a-budget size constraint

verifier_notes: CalibForge software-engineering_*_026 is a whole family of the exact TB2.1 template ('I have a decoder at /app/X reading stdin; write me a file <=N bytes that decodes to target'); all sampled are graded ok/strong, none FREE, except the TBKV one software-engineering_20260612_191200_026 (FREE) which I excluded. No packet-vs-verifier_strength grade conflicts among my final_top10. All Recursive-Task-Synthesis entries are 'absent' (no verifier ships) and none is close enough to enter final_top10 given the graded CalibForge/TMax equivalents. TerminalWorld's two best skill matches here, tw_11733 (decompress embedded SWF) and tw_116487 (create compressed archive), are FREE-graded and kept in per_source only.

notes: The new corpora dominate. CalibForge is decisive: it ships a whole software-engineering_*_026 family that is the TB2.1 template verbatim - 'I have a decoder/deserializer at /app/X reading stdin; write me a file <=N bytes that decodes to target' - with tight byte budgets and ok/strong verifiers, so seven of the final ten are CalibForge and would be more if not for balance. TMax is the second pillar: task_000185 (reverse a stripped unpacker to produce a file it accepts under a size budget) is a near-exact match, and TMax has deep custom-compression/RLE and reverse-a-format-from-its-binary tasks. Terminal-Lego only reaches binary-serialization adjacency (write floats to binary, DER parse) - no format-reversing or size-budget content. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has crackme-RE and encrypt/validate-magic-bytes roundtrip tasks that touch the skill but every one is graded 'absent' and none is close enough to displace the graded CalibForge/TMax matches. TerminalWorld's closest matches (Singularity image shrink, ESIL binary emulation) are decent but its very best - decompress embedded SWF, create compressed archive - are FREE. SWE-Smith/Rebench reach only codec/serialization adjacency (cantools bit-packing, aiohttp ZLibCompressor, chardet, cloudpickle) with mismatched task_form. Downstream merge: the CalibForge _026 family plus TMax task_000185 are the gold; everything else is supporting.
